title: Large Pre-trained Language Models Contain Human-like Biases of What is Right and Wrong to Do
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the model's alignment with human-perceived moral norms for various actions. In relation to faith/religion, it specifically measures whether the model considers the action 'go to church' as a normative (morally positive) behavior.
findings: The model (BERT) rates the action 'go to church' with a positive moral score, categorizing it as a 'Do' (a normative action) alongside actions like 'eat healthy' and 'be a good person'. This reflects that the model learned a bias from its training data where this religious activity is portrayed as socially positive.
